text: Well, they are actually no different from people who hold two employee jobs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The employee will also make two streams of contributions from the two jobs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Keep in mind, however, that for all members, there is a cap on total CPF contributions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SEPs who are concurrently regular employees will not need to contribute beyond this cap if they make an application to CPF Board.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, if they want to cap it and treat it as though he was one regular employee only, they can apply to do that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will also study Assoc Prof Walter Theseira's suggestion on allowing SEPs to vary CAYE contribution rates according to their income peaks and troughs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I must say that I find that a very interesting idea.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Let us study how we can implement it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are simply breaking up the contributions into smaller, more manageable parts as and when the SEPs earn.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Only a small proportion of SEPs are part of the pilot.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These SEPs can choose to opt out and set the CAYE contribution rate to zero if they have contributed to their MediSave in full or are keeping up under an instalment plan.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have also not taken a decision whether to extend CAYE any further.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will always welcome feedback on how to make our CPF system better.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, I would like to thank Members of Parliament who shared their feedback on the Retirement Sum Scheme (RSS).

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Zainal Sapari asked if members could have the option to end their payouts even earlier than what it is today.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Shorter payout durations mean higher payouts but this comes at the expense of increased risk of outliving those payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In 2018, more than half of Singapore residents aged 65 were expected to live past 85 years old.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This means that if RSS payouts ended just after 20 years, at age 85, more than half – the majority – of RSS members may have no CPF payouts for their remaining lives.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In comparison, extending RSS payouts until age 90 at most will protect up to two in three members from outliving their payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This provides a reasonable level of assurance for members, while still increasing their payout amount as compared to the current RSS rules.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members also have the option of joining CPF LIFE before the age of 80 if they are personally worried about outliving their RSS payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To Members of the House, I seek your help to reassure your residents of the following, that there is no change to when they can receive their RSS payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Those who are 65 today can instruct CPF Board to start their payouts anytime.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: No one will get a lower payout than they are already receiving.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The CPF caters to 3.9 million members, and 150,000 employers interact with it regularly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Most members at different times of their lives interact with CPF Board on housing, healthcare and retirement matters.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They may also use their CPF savings for investment, education and insurance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On top of all that, members may be included in the many Government schemes administered by CPF Board on behalf of other agencies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Such schemes include the Workfare Income Supplement, Silver Support Scheme, MediShield Life, Goods and Services Tax Vouchers and so on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the same time, CPF rules have to evolve to stay relevant.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Quite often, new rules have to co-exist with old ones to honour commitments to older members.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As a result, even when family members compare notes, they may get confused.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is done at three levels: through mass media channels; segmented outreach; and direct personalised communications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: CPF Board uses multiple media channels to reach out to as many Singaporeans as possible and increase their understanding of CPF.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Board conducts regular campaigns, including in vernacular languages, to clarify details of schemes, such as nominations and top-ups.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Board also uses social media to share bite-sized information with followers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Besides Facebook and Instagram posts, video series explain retirement issues in a light-hearted, easy-to-digest manner.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Board tailors its content to the needs of various groups.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ground outreach in the heartlands is especially important.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, many of us would have seen CPF Board's Retirement Planning Roadshows in our neighbourhood centre or mall.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To further expand its reach, CPF Board also works with other agencies and grassroots organisations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In 2019 alone, CPF Board conducted over 60 engagement sessions for more than 6,000 grassroots leaders (GRLs) and residents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Board trained 300 GRLs in 2019, enabling them to reach out to more than 3,000 residents right in their neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Dr Maliki Mohamad, for example, has personally conducted 10 sessions in Siglap and engages his audience with flipchart diagrams and slides.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think this must be continuing in the good tradition of former Minister Lim Swee Say who was just here earlier.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He also conducted many sessions in the whole of Bedok area where he serves as a Member of Parliament.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Foo Mee Har has personally done six briefings this year alone in Ayer Rajah.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Pillai and Ms Sim Ann have actively supported CPF ground engagements in Bukit Batok and Bukit Timah.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I personally have done more than 20 sessions in Bishan North and joined in sessions organised by advisors like Er Dr Lee Bee Wah.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These sessions go a long way in educating the public about CPF schemes that are relevant to them and clarify their doubts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: CPF Board also conducts talks that target member segments, such as young members who have just started work, the self-employed and employers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The talks cover topics that are most relevant to each group, such as housing matters for young members who are purchasing their first homes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To provide members some idea of the materials available, CPF Board has compiled information packs which are available for your collection in the Parliament Library.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Thirdly, besides mass media and segmented outreach, CPF Board uses direct personalised communications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Many members still prefer one-on-one discussions about their specific circumstances.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For most members, their first point of contact will remain one of our five CPF Service Centres in Bishan, Jurong, Maxwell, Tampines and Woodlands.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On average, that is nearly 800 every day at every service centre.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Staff at these service centres are equipped to engage members in vernacular languages, even in some dialects.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To bring CPF services nearer to members, especially the elderly, CPF Board sets up mobile service centres.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These mobile centres move around to a new heartland location, usually the Community Centre (CC) or library, every two months.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members can make enquiries and perform a range of CPF transactions without having to travel to a service centre.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In 2019, mobile service centres were set up at six locations – Kampong Chai Chee CC, Yew Tee CC, Geylang Serai CC, Bukit Merah CC, Toa Payoh Library and the one currently running at Potong Pasir CC until the end of this year and, of course, Nee Soon CC can be considered, too.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For those who prefer phone clarifications, they can contact the CPF call centre.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The call centre is staffed by experienced CPF officers who can manage queries in a variety of languages.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Other communications that go directly to members, such as the package members receive at age 55, or letters on their RSS or CPF LIFE payouts, have been simplified and enhanced over the years.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Where the member is required to take action, this is clearly indicated for the member's attention.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For members reaching milestone ages, CPF Board provides personalised face-to-face guidance as part of the CPF Retirement Planning Service.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is available to members turning 54 or reaching their payout eligibility age of 65.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members who have attended these sessions found it very helpful.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will also link these members up with other Government agencies, if necessary, such as the Social Service Offices, HDB or the Ministry of Health.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In summary, Deputy Speaker, communicating CPF has been and will remain a top priority for us.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We welcome suggestions from Members of the House on how we can do better.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With this, Deputy Speaker, I hope that I have addressed Members' questions and suggestions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And with your permission, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: There were suggestions that taxi operators and so on should start to pay for PML premiums on behalf of drivers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I wonder what is the Ministry's take on this compulsory arrangement that some had suggested.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Would it, therefore, lead to an increase in, say, for example, rental cost of the vehicles?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Will it lead to an increase in fare structure because the operator will essentially find a way to transfer this or the premium somewhere else?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I wonder what is the Ministry's thinking about some of these suggestions that were made.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Deputy Speaker, I thank Mr Ang Hin Kee for following up on this suggestion.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Ang knows the taxi drivers very well.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think he fully understands that when the issue of PML insurance was raised in discussions with them, the issue of cost and who will bear it, was prominent in their minds.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Ang is correct to point out that the cost has to be carried by someone.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Keep in mind the vast majority of SEPs, including taxi drivers and private hire car drivers, have chosen this livelihood as a preference.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Deputy Speaker, just a quick response to the Minister's question.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: I am going to echo my fellow Assoc Prof Walter Theseira and say that, yes, in the goodness of time.
